NKE.rationale: NKE is experiencing severe fundamental deterioration across all key metrics: EPS down 35% YoY to $0.35, operating margin collapsed to 5.8% (lowest in the observed window), operating cash flow down 76% YoY, and gross margin compressed to 40.2% driven by tariff headwinds. The stock trades at 29.5x PE on sharply declining earnings, offering no premium over the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.34%. Multiple analyst downgrades (HSBC to Hold, BofA to Neutral) and S&P's negative outlook revision confirm the deteriorating trajectory. While Nike's brand franchise remains strong, the turnaround is early-stage with Q4 guidance calling for further revenue decline and margin pressure. The combination of collapsing earnings, elevated valuation on those earnings, and near-term downside catalysts (tariff headwinds, China structural decline, oil cost pressure) creates a strongly negative risk-reward profile.

Operating margin collapsed to ~5.8% from 7.5% YoY, lowest in observed window
Operating cash flow down 76% YoY to $430M from $1.79B
Gross margin compressed to 40.2% reflecting ~300bps tariff impact in North America
PE diluted 29.5x on 2026-04-23, earnings yield 3.4% below 10-year Treasury at 4.34%

HSBC downgraded to Hold, cut price target from $90 to $48
Bank of America downgraded to Neutral flagging oil price risk to product costs

Stock down 31.6% over prior quarter to $44.78, just 6.4% above 365-day low of $42.09
